facts.raw_span: A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm
A 52-year-old man presented with a progressively enlarging, mildly tender right-flank subcutaneous nodule noted over two years
an ~8×4 cm subcutaneous mass over the right hypochondriac and flank regions
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 (largest 3.5 cm) and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib measuring 8×4×4 cm

concepts.why: The patient has a history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and the current presentation of a subcutaneous mass and multiple nodules in the liver and lung is consistent with extrahepatic metastasis.
The presence of a subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib and the patient's history of cancer treatment suggest the possibility of a primary soft tissue sarcoma.
The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on CT scan is consistent with pulmonary metastasis from a primary cancer such as hepatocellular carcinoma.
The presence of multiple nodules in the liver on CT scan is consistent with liver metastasis from a primary cancer such as hepatocellular carcinoma.
The patient has a history of hepatocellular carcinoma and the current presentation of multiple nodules in the liver is consistent with recurrence of the primary cancer.

The presence of a subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib and the patient's history of cancer treatment suggest the possibility of soft tissue metastasis from a primary cancer such as hepatocellular carcinoma.

The presence of a subcutaneous mass invading the 12th rib and the patient's history of cancer treatment suggest the possibility of rib metastasis from a primary cancer such as hepatocellular carcinoma.

The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on CT scan is consistent with lung cancer, although the patient's history of hepatocellular carcinoma suggests that these nodules may be metastatic.

rationales.F01: The presence of a progressively enlarging subcutaneous nodule is more typical of a metastatic lesion or a primary soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F06: The presence of a large subcutaneous mass is more typical of a metastatic lesion or a primary soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F10: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels are highly suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules is more typical of metastatic disease, which could be from hepatocellular carcinoma or another primary tumor.
rationales.F12: The presence of multiple nodules in the liver and a soft tissue mass invading the rib is highly suggestive of metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma and elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels, combined with the presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and a right-flank soft tissue mass, support the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma with extrahepatic metastasis.
